Cisco Beach, Madaket Beach, and Surfside Beach. Nantucket Conservation Foundation permits required. $200 to $1,800.
Nantucket private property — many family compounds. Covers premium tent, restrooms, generator, and Nantucket town permits.

Most wine country couples shop in San Francisco for designer gowns at Mark Ingram Atelier SF, Carine's Bridal Atelier, or Lovely Bride SF, where Vera Wang, Carolina Herrera, Inbal Dror, and Galia Lahav designer gowns run $5,000 to $15,000-plus. Professional alterations ($500 to $900), wine country hair and makeup ($500 to $1,000+ on-site bridal packages â€” Joy notes basic hair and makeup starts at $500 with on-site bridal packages $1,000+), and partner attire bring total designer-tier attire and beauty spend to $7,500 to $22,000.

San Francisco and Napa boutiques carry mid-to-upper boutique gowns from $2,500 to $5,500 with personalized styling. Wine country hair and makeup ($400 to $700 per session reflecting destination pricing) and partner attire bring boutique-tier total to $3,500 to $8,500.

San Francisco sample sales and online platforms including Still White provide boutique gowns at 40 to 70 percent off retail. Mid-range hair and makeup from wine country salons or traveling stylists runs $250 to $400 each. Total mid-range attire and beauty for both partners runs $1,200 to $3,500.

David's Bridal locations in the broader Bay Area, online retailers from Azazie and ASOS Wedding offer dresses from $150 to $600. SF Men's Wearhouse and Indochino San Francisco cover suit rental and made-to-measure from $200 to $700. Appropriate for elopements at small vineyard venues, Napa County courthouse ceremonies, and small private property gatherings.

Premium spirits, craft cocktails, and full estate wine service. Wine country weddings differ fundamentally from other markets â€” wine is the experiential centerpiece, with curated estate wines at every winery venue setting the tone. Many wineries require minimum wine spend (Viansa requires $35 per drinking-age guest as their minimum). A premium bar package layered onto estate wine runs $85 to $130 per head for a five-hour reception. California requires RBS-certified bartenders.

Mid-shelf spirits, comprehensive estate wine pours (the wine is the star of every wine country wedding), and craft beer from Napa-Sonoma breweries â€” Russian River Brewing Company in Santa Rosa (the legendary Pliny the Elder brewery), Lagunitas in Petaluma, Bear Republic Brewing in Healdsburg, and Sonoma County's broader craft beer scene â€” on full pour. Standard open bar service for a five-hour reception runs $60 to $90 per person.

Beer and wine service without spirits. This tier is conceptually unusual in wine country â€” most wineries center wine as the entire beverage program, with beer as supplement rather than alternative. A curated estate wine program (typically including white, red, sparkling, and rosÃ© pours) supplemented with regional craft beer runs $38 to $60 per person. The estate wine inclusion at winery venues often eliminates separate "bar" costs entirely; beer-only supplementation is the typical add-on.

No alcohol service. Genuinely uncommon in wine country (the entire region's identity centers on wine culture) but available for couples whose religious traditions or personal preferences exclude alcohol. Most winery venues actively discourage dry weddings since wine service is central to their business model. Non-alcoholic options â€” local Napa Valley Coffee Roasting Company coffee, premium sparkling cider from wine country producers, and specialty mocktails â€” run $8 to $18 per person. Many winery venues won't accommodate dry receptions; verify before booking.

White-glove plated service built around Napa Valley's culinary identity, which represents one of America's deepest concentrations of Michelin-starred restaurants and James Beard Foundation award winners. Auberge du Soleil and other top-tier venues offer Michelin Star culinary teams. Wine pairings, multi-course tastings, and the elevated California cuisine tradition shape every menu. Top wine country caterers operate at $175 to $285 per head for full-service plated dining before California sales tax and the standard 22 to 24 percent service charge.

A full plated or family-style seated dinner with professional staffing. Wine country mid-market catering remains meaningfully above California averages because of vendor competition for major estate venues. Standalone seated dinner catering through established wine country caterers runs $125 to $185 per head before sales tax and service charges. Plan for one server per 10-15 guests and one bartender per 100 guests.

Buffet and family-style service â€” including farm-to-table California spreads from wine country's extraordinary local agriculture, pasta bar stations (starting around $40 per person), grill packages ($35 to $48 per person), and elevated taco bars ($30 per person). Wine country buffet pricing runs above urban California markets because of vendor travel costs and the elevated competition for premium estate venues. Mid-market buffet catering runs $80 to $125 per head.

Heavy appetizers and food stations â€” California small plates featuring wine country produce, charcuterie boards with Bellwether Farms cheese and Marin Sun Farms meats, Dungeness crab from the nearby coast, and passed cocktail bites paired with estate wines. Cocktail receptions in wine country typically run alongside extensive wine service rather than full bar service.

A backyard or family property gathering where food comes from beloved Napa-Sonoma institutions â€” Oxbow Public Market vendors, Model Bakery in St. Helena, Boon Fly Cafe at Carneros Resort, or a Sonoma County farm-to-table caterer at the most accessible price point. For anything at Auberge du Soleil, Four Seasons, V. Sattui, or major winery venues with exclusive catering requirements (which most wine country venues maintain), this tier isn't available.

Top wine country floral studios specializing in elaborate vineyard installations, ceremony arches integrating estate-grown blooms and locally foraged greenery, ceiling treatments, and full tablescapes. Joy notes wine country florists typically need a $10,000 minimum before labor and taxes. Simple designs start $12,000-$15,000; elaborate installations exceed $20,000. Specialty rentals like lounge vignettes and wall installations add $5,000+. Couture programs at Auberge or Four Seasons-level celebrations with multiple installation pieces run $35,000 to $65,000.

Large-scale floral design with a wine country aesthetic â€” locally grown garden roses, dahlias from Sonoma County flower farms, olive branches from estate olive groves, lavender and rosemary from Provence-style landscaping, and the warm-tone Mediterranean palette that defines wine country wedding florals. Full installation work at winery venues runs $14,000 to $28,000.

The full complement of wedding florals with a wine country character: bridal bouquet of California garden roses, ranunculus, and seasonal blooms with eucalyptus and olive branch accents, ceremony arrangements, and reception centerpieces (typical centerpieces run $100-$150 each at mid-market). A full traditional package at a Napa-Sonoma venue runs $5,500 to $11,000 â€” meaningfully above urban California averages due to vendor travel and destination pricing.

A scaled-back floral plan paired with the inherent decor of wine country venues â€” Madrona Manor's 8 acres of romantic gardens, vineyard rows, olive groves, and rolling hills. Simple eucalyptus and olive branch runners, candles, and a few statement arrangements with locally grown roses complement the natural setting without requiring full installation.

Dried California wildflowers, preserved olive branches and eucalyptus, locally grown garden roses sourced direct from Sonoma County flower farms, and arrangements assembled at home. The Petaluma flower farms (the broader Sonoma County is a major California flower-growing region) offer accessible direct purchase. For a small ceremony at a public garden or private property, minimal florals feel intentional given wine country's natural beauty.

A full 10 to 12-piece band with vocalist, horn section, and full rhythm section. Wine country wedding entertainment costs run meaningfully above San Francisco market rates due to band travel premiums and the destination-wedding demand for booked-out summer Saturdays. Top wedding bands serving Auberge, Four Seasons, and major estate venues run $18,000 to $30,000 at the marquee level. Music cutoffs at most Napa Valley venues are 10 or 11 PM due to county noise ordinances.

A full reception band of 6 to 8 musicians. San Francisco Bay Area wedding bands routinely travel to wine country for $9,000 to $17,000 packages reflecting destination-level pricing. The SF Bay Area musician depth (Bay Area Symphony freelance community, the strong San Francisco jazz scene) means wine country has access to extraordinary talent.

A string quartet, jazz trio, or acoustic duo for the ceremony and cocktail hour paired with a DJ for the reception. A live duo for ceremony and cocktail hour runs around $750-$1,500 alone; the full ceremony plus reception DJ combination runs $2,500 to $6,500. Wine country's acoustic Mediterranean atmosphere supports ceremony-only live music followed by DJ-driven reception dancing.

A professional wedding DJ for the full reception. Most wine country DJs charge between $1,500 to $2,500 at the broader market level; established destination-experienced DJs serving major estate venues run $2,000 to $4,500.

A curated playlist managed by a trusted friend through a venue-provided or rented sound system. Works for intimate elopements at small vineyard properties, micro-weddings under 30 guests, and small backyard gatherings. For anything at major estate venues with sound system requirements and amplified music restrictions, this tier typically isn't permitted.

Lead photographer, second photographer, and a cinematographer producing a feature film and highlight reel â€” with engagement session and premium album. Top wine country editorial photographers serving Auberge du Soleil, Four Seasons Napa, and Beaulieu Garden-level celebrations run $16,000 to $28,000 for the complete package. Napa-Sonoma is among America's most photogenic wedding destinations, with vineyard rows at golden hour, hilltop overlooks, barrel rooms, and olive allÃ©es all rewarding photographers with destination-level expertise.

Lead photographer, second shooter, and full videography with feature film and highlight reel. Full-team luxury packages at established wine country venues run $9,500 to $16,000. Many premier Napa-Sonoma photographers maintain destination-wedding pricing structures reflecting the deep luxury market.

A strong lead photographer paired with a highlight film videographer. Mid-market wine country packages including full-day photography and a three- to five-minute highlight film run $6,500 to $11,000 with skilled local talent.

A single experienced photographer, full-day coverage, no video. Experienced wine country wedding photographers who know vineyard light conditions, the specific photo opportunities at major estates, and the technical demands of destination weddings run $4,500 to $8,000.

A trusted friend or a newer photographer building their portfolio. Works for intimate elopements at small vineyard properties, micro-weddings at boutique venues, and small ceremonies at the Napa County Clerk's office. For anything at Auberge, Four Seasons, or comparable wine country landmark venues, a professional photographer with destination-level experience is functionally required by venue standards.

Full-service planning in wine country. Destination wedding planners managing celebrations at Auberge, Four Seasons, and major Napa-Sonoma estates run $12,000 to $28,000. Most wine country couples plan from out of town and require comprehensive local expertise. Many established wine country planners (Lovely Day Events, Blissful Events) charge 10 to 15 percent of overall wedding budget â€” and on $100,000-$200,000+ wedding budgets, planning fees alone routinely run five figures.

Partial planning for couples who have booked their venue but need substantial local expertise for vendor sourcing, contract review, and on-the-ground destination logistics. Even at partial planning, wine country expertise commands premium pricing due to the destination wedding complexity and the high stakes of major venue logistics.

Day-of coordination for any wine country venue. Most major Napa-Sonoma venues explicitly require a professional planner â€” venues like Viansa state "we require a dedicated wedding planner and a professional caterer" in their booking requirements. Standalone day-of coordination runs $2,800 to $6,000.

No professional planning or coordination. Realistic only for intimate elopements at non-winery venues, micro-weddings at private properties, and small ceremonies of 20 or fewer guests. For anything at a major Napa-Sonoma winery or estate venue, the absence of a professional planner is functionally impossible â€” most venues require one as a contract condition.

Bespoke letterpress or foil-stamped suites from Bay Area boutique paper designers specializing in wine country aesthetics: vineyard and grape leaf botanicals, olive branch motifs, lavender and rosemary illustrations, Mediterranean color palettes, and hand-lettered calligraphy on cotton stock. Most wine country couples commission custom invitations through San Francisco studios. A fully custom letterpress suite runs $2,200 to $6,500.

Semi-custom and designer-template suites from Minted (the San Francisco-based company), Zola, or Artifact Uprising. A standard digitally printed suite of 100 sets runs $537 to $783 on Minted. Add save-the-dates and day-of paper goods, and a full package runs $500 to $2,200.

Paperless Post, Zola's digital invite tools, or a custom digital invite. Increasingly common in wine country's tech-adjacent professional couple market. Free platforms available; Paperless Post premium designs run $1 to $3 per send.

Word of mouth, a free Zola or The Knot wedding website, and personal outreach. Appropriate for elopements, micro-weddings, and intimate family gatherings. A California marriage license costs $86 in Napa County or $113 in Sonoma County, valid for 90 days â€” California has no waiting period before the ceremony, allowing for same-day marriage.

Auberge du Soleil in Rutherford (the Michelin-starred Napa Valley icon, with full venue buyouts running well into six figures), Four Seasons Resort and Residences Napa Valley (packages range $58,185 to $154,591 with a $45,000 minimum spend), The Estate Yountville (packages $26,054 to $162,272 with indoor space up to 700 guests), and Meadowood Napa Valley anchor the iconic landmark tier. These are the venues that define Napa Valley as America's premier destination wedding market. Full property buyouts are typical for weekend dates. Napa County's Winery Definition Ordinance restricts weddings at vineyards built after 1974, making landmark estates particularly valuable.

V. Sattui Winery in St. Helena (May 2025 pricing $28,591 to $71,643 with $12,950 minimum spend, 6-hour events ending by 11:00 PM), Beaulieu Garden in Rutherford (an iconic 1880s Mediterranean-style estate), Tre Posti (a converted 1880s farmhouse and winery in St. Helena), Carneros Resort and Spa, and BR Cohn Winery in Sonoma operate in this estate tier. Private full-property estate venues run $35,000 to $75,000 in site fees, before catering, rentals, and the substantial F&B minimums that anchor most Napa packages.

The Meritage Resort and Spa in Napa (three-course dinners starting $87-$89 per person, with full venue capability), Vintage House at Yountville, Calistoga Ranch (an Auberge Resort), and Solage Calistoga (Auberge) anchor the grand hotel tier in wine country. The North Block Hotel in Yountville and Andaz Napa downtown bring smaller-scale luxury options. California's 7.75 to 9.6 percent Napa County sales tax plus 22 to 24 percent service charges apply to all F&B â€” a meaningful addition on top of already-elevated wine country per-head pricing.

Madrona Manor in Healdsburg (1881 Victorian estate on 8 acres in Dry Creek Valley, peak season fees from $1,500, in-house Michelin star chef catering required at added cost), MacArthur Place Hotel & Spa in Sonoma, Las Alcobas Napa Valley, and the Wine Country Inn round out the boutique tier. These properties bring all-suite hotel character at meaningfully lower price points than the resort tier while maintaining wine country luxury.

Cornerstone Sonoma (a marketplace with gardens), Healdsburg's Trentadue Winery, Lodi-area wineries (south of Sonoma but accessible), and Highlands Estate in Cloverdale (a 21-acre private weekend property surrounded by Syrah vineyards, $6,600-$7,500 for Saturday peak weddings of 100 guests with bring-your-own vendor model) operate in this tier. Many wine country dedicated venues offer turnkey packages bundling venue time, tables, chairs, baseline staffing, and rentals.

Wine country's industrial-style venues are rarer than urban markets, but Sonoma County's converted barns and the artisan venues of Petaluma, Geyserville, and Healdsburg offer rustic-industrial alternatives. Mountain House Estate in Cloverdale ($6,500 peak reception fee, $1,500 ceremony) is a strong representative of this category. The blank-canvas wine country venue tier supports couples wanting more design flexibility than turnkey winery packages allow.

Napa Valley's restaurant scene is one of America's deepest â€” The French Laundry, Bouchon, Auberge du Soleil's restaurant, Press Restaurant in St. Helena, and Bottega Yountville (Michael Chiarello) all have strong private dining and buyout capability. Sonoma's restaurant scene through Single Thread Farms in Healdsburg (3 Michelin stars) and the broader Healdsburg food scene offers equally strong options. F&B minimums apply, often $15,000 to $30,000-plus for full restaurant buyouts.

Bothe-Napa Valley State Park, Sugarloaf Ridge State Park in Sonoma, Robert Louis Stevenson State Park, and the California State Park system's wine country properties permit ceremony events with advance coordination. Cornerstone Sonoma's gardens, Quarryhill Botanical Garden in Glen Ellen, and the Napa Valley Hike & Bike Trail offer ceremony permit possibilities. Permit fees through California State Parks and Napa County run $500 to $3,500 depending on location, day, and party size. Required insurance and rentals not included.

A family property in St. Helena, Yountville, Healdsburg, or one of wine country's residential communities. Napa-Sonoma residential properties often include vineyard frontage, olive groves, and the Mediterranean architecture that rivals any paid venue. Budget covers tent rental (genuinely substantial in wine country â€” Standard Party Rentals and BBJ La Tavola specialize in destination-level rentals), portable luxury restroom trailers, generator access, full power infrastructure, and any required Napa County or Sonoma County permits. Backyard wedding totals can climb sharply when guest counts exceed 50 due to infrastructure costs.

Nashville's bridal boutique scene has grown significantly with the city's rise as a wedding destination. Cynthia Rose Bridal in Green Hills and Little White Dress carry designer gowns from Vera Wang, Monique Lhuillier, and similar houses, with gowns starting at $3,000 and running well above $10,000 for couture labels. Add professional alterations ($300 to $600), bridal hair and makeup ($300 to $500 per session at Nashville's top studios), and partner attire, and total attire and beauty spend in this tier runs $5,000 to $15,000.

The working center of Nashville's bridal market. White Traditions Bridal House in Franklin and Carrie Karibo Bridal in Nashville's Germantown neighborhood carry a strong range of boutique gowns from $1,500 to $4,000, with professional alterations and personalized styling included in the appointment experience. Nashville's hair and makeup community is deep â€” Heck Designs notes bridal hair and makeup typically costs $300 to $500 for the bride including a trial. Total boutique-tier attire and beauty for both partners runs $2,500 to $6,000.

Nashville's annual bridal sample sales and online platforms like Still White and PreOwned Wedding Dresses give budget-conscious brides access to boutique gowns at 40 to 70 percent off retail. A $3,000 gown purchased as a sample for $900 plus professional alterations at a local seamstress totals far less than a new gown. Mid-range hair and makeup salons in East Nashville and Germantown run $150 to $250 each for styling. Total mid-range attire spend for both partners runs $1,000 to $2,800.

David's Bridal on Gallatin Pike starts under $500 for ready-to-wear gowns. Online retailers including Azazie and ASOS Wedding offer dresses from $150 to $600 with free returns. Suit rental from Men's Wearhouse or Friar Tux runs $200 to $300. Self-done or budget-salon beauty keeps the total in range. Particularly appropriate for backyard weddings, elopements, and small farm ceremonies where the register is genuinely casual and the setting does the visual work.

Premium spirits, craft cocktails, Tennessee whiskey flights, and curated wine on full pour for the reception. Nashville's bar culture â€” bourbon-forward, with strong craft beer and wine options â€” makes this tier feel locally rooted rather than generic. The Loveless Barn's premium bar packages and similar all-inclusive venue bar options run in this range. Expect a signature cocktail hour with passed drinks, followed by full bar service through the reception. Tennessee's liquor laws require licensed bartenders for all alcohol service; budget for that staffing within the per-head rate.

Mid-shelf spirits, a solid Tennessee whiskey or bourbon selection, house wine, and domestic and craft beer. The standard open bar package at most Nashville venues and outside bar service companies. Wedding.report puts Nashville bar costs at roughly 15 to 20 percent of total catering spend; for a mid-range wedding, this tier covers full open bar service for a five-hour reception at a price that doesn't dominate the budget.

Beer and wine service with non-alcoholic options. A common choice at Tennessee church-adjacent venues and family-oriented receptions. Nashville's craft beer scene â€” Bearded Iris in Germantown, Tennessee Brew Works in SoBro â€” gives a beer-and-wine bar genuine personality if you curate the selection. Budget $28 to $42 per person for a professionally managed beer and wine bar through a licensed bartending service.

No alcohol service. Common in Nashville's faith community and for certain venue types â€” Foundry Events on Clinton Street, for instance, has a no-alcohol policy. Non-alcoholic options range from sweet tea and lemonade stations (very Nashville) to craft mocktail menus built around Tennessee sorghum and seasonal fruits. Budget covers non-alcoholic beverage service and bartender fees for a dry bar setup.

White-glove plated service with a chef-driven Southern menu â€” think heritage pork tenderloin, buttermilk-brined chicken, and seasonal vegetables from Middle Tennessee farms. Flavor Catering and Chef's Market are among Nashville's most respected full-service wedding caterers, known for elevated comfort food that still feels like Nashville. At this tier, expect tableside service, a dedicated captain, and a staffing ratio of one server per ten guests. Heck Designs & Photography's Nashville market data puts full-service catering at the high end of the $60 to $120 per person range; top-tier plated dinners with premium menus run $110 to $160 per head before service charges and Tennessee's 9.25 percent sales tax.

A full seated dinner with professional service â€” two or three courses, staffed tables, and a menu that reflects Nashville's farm-to-table moment. G Catering and similar mid-market Nashville caterers run in this range. Family-style service has become the dominant format at Nashville's barn and estate venues, where shared platters of Southern comfort food feel natural and guests tend to linger longer at the table. Wedding.report data puts Nashville catering at $81 to $102 per person on average; this tier covers the upper half of that range.

Buffet and family-style service at Nashville's most popular barn and estate venues. The Loveless Barn's in-house catering â€” famous biscuits, Southern comfort dishes, and a menu built around what makes Nashville food worth traveling for â€” operates in this range, and it's one of the best catering values in the city. Most Nashville venues with in-house catering bundle this into their overall package pricing. For outside caterers, budget $55 to $80 per person for buffet service before gratuity and tax.

Heavy appetizers and food stations rather than a seated meal. Popular for the younger Nashville wedding market and for couples hosting at East Nashville lofts or downtown event spaces where the format fits the venue's energy. Local food trucks â€” Nashville has a strong food truck scene â€” typically charge $1,000 to $2,500 flat for wedding service and bring significant personality to a cocktail-style reception. Budget $40 to $60 per person for a caterer-managed station setup.

A family property or backyard wedding where the food is community-sourced, potluck-adjacent, or handled by a trusted local restaurant doing drop-off catering. Nashville's accessibility to grocery infrastructure and its strong culture of church suppers and community gatherings makes this feel natural in the right context. Food trucks in the $1,000 to $1,500 flat-fee range are the cleanest execution of this tier for a small wedding. For anything over 75 guests at a formal venue, most Nashville venues with in-house catering requirements make this tier moot.

Full-scale transformation of Nashville's estate and barn venues by the city's most celebrated floral studios â€” ceiling installations in the Loveless Barn's chandelier-hung main hall, elaborate ceremony arches against Cheekwood's garden walls, and full tablescapes with tall centerpieces using rare imported blooms. Studios at this level carry $12,000+ minimums for Cheekwood-level event work.

Large-scale floral design that transforms Nashville's estate and barn venues â€” ceremony arches against Cheekwood's garden walls, lush tablescapes, full reception florals. Skilled Nashville studios with strong Riverwood Mansion and estate venue portfolios run $12,000 to $21,000.

The full complement of classic wedding florals: bridal bouquet, bridesmaids' bouquets, boutonnieres, a ceremony arch, and reception centerpieces. Heck Designs & Photography puts Nashville florists at $2,500 to $5,000 average; for a full traditional package at a mid-size reception, the realistic spend is $4,000 to $10,000 depending on bloom selection and guest count. Nashville's proximity to Tennessee wildflowers and Appalachian greenery makes garden-inspired and organic designs particularly strong here.

A scaled-back floral plan paired with non-floral decor rentals â€” Edison string lights (ubiquitous at Nashville barn venues), lanterns, wood farm tables, and fabric draping. Many of Nashville's barn venues include basic string lighting in the rental fee, which reduces the decoration burden significantly. Local rental companies stock the warmly lit, rustic-elegant pieces that define Middle Tennessee's wedding aesthetic. A bridal bouquet, boutonniere, and a few ceremony arrangements alongside solid rentals can produce a beautiful result in this range.

Dried pampas grass, eucalyptus, Tennessee wildflowers, or fully DIY florals sourced from Nashville Farmers Market or the Wholesale District. Nashville's country aesthetic makes dried and greenery-forward arrangements feel intentional rather than budget-driven. For couples with a creative family network and a rustic venue that doesn't need much dressing, this tier produces genuinely beautiful results at a fraction of the full-florist cost.

Nashville is Music City, and at this tier you access the deepest live wedding entertainment talent pool in America. A full 10 to 12-piece band â€” vocalist, rhythm section, full horns â€” drawing from musicians who perform at The Bluebird Cafe and on Lower Broadway. Heck Designs puts the upper end of Nashville bands at $10,000-plus; $14,000 to $20,000 is where the marquee acts with touring-level production specs begin. Book 12 months out for October.

A full reception band of 6 to 8 musicians in Nashville, where the talent pool is deeper and the quality ceiling higher than almost anywhere in the country. Heck Designs puts Nashville live bands at $4,000 to $10,000-plus; premium acts with strong wedding entertainment reputations run $8,000 to $14,000. Book 12 months out for October Saturdays.

A string quartet, acoustic duo, or three-piece jazz ensemble for the ceremony and cocktail hour paired with a DJ for the reception. In Nashville, this format has a particular magic â€” a working singer-songwriter performing originals and covers during cocktail hour, then a DJ for the dance floor. Local acoustic acts typically run $800 to $2,000 for ceremony and cocktail coverage. Combined with a reception DJ, total entertainment spend lands in this tier.

A professional wedding DJ for the full reception. Heck Designs puts Nashville DJ costs at $1,500 to $6,000 depending on inclusions; Wedding.report's actual couple data shows Nashville DJ spend averaging $1,100 to $1,400 for a 125-guest wedding. A good Nashville wedding DJ understands the city's musical identity â€” you'll hear country, classic rock, and modern pop share a dance floor without it feeling jarring. Many Nashville DJs include MC services, basic uplighting, and sound system in their packages.

A curated Spotify or Apple Music playlist run through a venue-provided or rented sound system, managed by a trusted friend. Works well for intimate receptions at CafÃ© at Thistle Farms, small barn ceremonies, or backyard gatherings where the vibe is more community gathering than production. Many Nashville barn venues include basic sound systems in their rental fee. Budget covers any speaker or PA rental needed beyond what the venue provides.

Lead photographer, second photographer, and a cinematographer producing a feature film. Nashville's most sought-after wedding photographers â€” those who work regularly at Cheekwood, Riverwood Mansion, and the Hermitage Hotel, and whose work appears in Nashville Lifestyles and Style Me Pretty â€” run $7,500 to $10,000. At this tier your photographer has pre-visualized the quality of Tennessee October light against a Cheekwood garden backdrop.

A lead photographer, second shooter, and videography team for a full Nashville wedding day. Wedding.report puts Nashville photography and video combined at $4,145 to $6,075; skilled Nashville teams with estate and barn venue portfolios run $5,500 to $7,500. A second shooter is particularly valuable at multi-space venues where ceremony and reception happen simultaneously.

A strong lead photographer paired with a highlight film videographer. Nashville's photography market is deep â€” the combination of a booming wedding industry and a large creative class means excellent talent at mid-market prices. Wedding.report's actual couple data puts Nashville photo and video spend at $4,145 to $5,066 for 125 guests; this tier covers the top of that range with both photo and video included. Full-day coverage, professionally edited gallery, and a three- to five-minute highlight film.

A single experienced photographer, full-day coverage, no video. Wedding.report's Nashville data shows solo photography averaging $2,600 to $3,200 for a 125-guest wedding, with upper-tier Nashville photographers running $3,500 to $4,500. For couples who prioritize photos over video and are working with a single, well-chosen location, solo coverage captures everything that matters. Albums and engagement sessions are typically add-ons.

A trusted friend with a capable camera, or a newer photographer building their portfolio. Nashville's large arts and music community means there are genuinely talented amateur photographers in most social circles. For intimate ceremonies, backyard weddings, and elopements in Tennessee's state parks, this works. For a 150-person reception at Cheekwood or The Loveless Barn, the risk â€” no backup equipment, no professional editing workflow, no experience managing a full wedding day timeline â€” is significant.

Full-service wedding planning in Nashville means working with firms like Modern Vintage Events, House of Grey Events, or Inspired Help â€” studios known for balancing the warmth of Southern wedding culture with tight logistics. Nashville's wedding boom has produced a strong planning market; full-service packages from experienced firms run $5,000 to $12,000. For estate and barn weddings where you're building everything from scratch â€” catering, tenting, lighting, vendors â€” a full-service planner is not a luxury but a necessity.

Partial planning covers vendor sourcing for remaining categories, contract review, timeline creation, and full day-of management. Particularly valuable in Nashville's market for couples who have booked their venue and photographer but need help navigating the strong-but-crowded vendor pool for florals, catering, and entertainment. Wedding.report puts Nashville planner costs at $2,700 to $4,600 on average; partial planning in this market runs at the lower end of that.

Day-of coordination is strongly recommended for any Nashville estate or barn wedding. When you're managing a tent, outside catering, a separate bar service, a band, and a florist across a multi-space property, someone needs to quarterback the timeline. Nashville's coordinator market is well-developed; experienced day-of coordinators run $1,200 to $2,800 depending on experience and the complexity of the event. Many Nashville venues that don't include in-house coordination will refer trusted local coordinators.

No professional planning or coordination. Realistic for intimate ceremonies at a family farm, a simple restaurant buyout, or a micro-wedding at a park with a small, local guest list. Nashville's strong community culture â€” church families, extended friend networks â€” means that for a small gathering, trusted people show up and make things work. For anything over 50 guests or involving more than four separate vendors, the absence of a coordinator creates meaningful day-of risk.

Bespoke letterpress or foil-stamped invitation suites from Nashville's boutique stationery designers â€” studios like Minted's Nashville-based designers and local shops in the Gulch and 12 South neighborhoods. Semi-custom and designer-template suites from Minted, Zola, or Artifact Uprising. A standard digitally printed suite of 100 invitation sets on Minted runs $537; foil-stamped runs $783. Paperless Post, Zola's free digital invite tools, or a custom-designed digital invite. Acme Feed and Seed on Lower Broadway, The CafÃ© at Thistle Farms in West Nashville, and Plot 41 Events on Clinton Street. A family farm in Franklin, Leiper's Fork, or the rolling hills of Williamson County. Budget covers tent rental ($1,500â€“$4,000), portable restrooms, generator access, and any required permits. The result is often the most personal wedding any guest attends.

New Orleans' bridal boutique market punches above its city-size weight. Premium spirits, craft cocktails built on Louisiana's rum and whiskey traditions, and New Orleans' extraordinary cocktail culture on full pour. Beer and wine service without spirits. A solid selection of Louisiana craft beer â€” Abita Amber, NOLA Brewing's Blonde Ale â€” and accessible wine gives a beer-and-wine bar local character. No alcohol service. Some faith community venues and historic properties have restrictions on alcohol service. Budget covers non-alcoholic beverage service and bartender setup fees.

New Orleans Creole cuisine at its finest: plated courses featuring Gulf seafood â€” shrimp, oysters, crab, redfish â€” prepared with French technique and Louisiana soul. Elysian Events Catering â€” specialists in New Orleans wedding catering since the 1970s â€” operates at this level, featuring miniature crab cakes, crawfish pies, and a Creole rice bar with chicken and andouille gumbo. Budget for Louisiana's 9.45 percent sales tax and the standard 18 to 22 percent service charge on top of the quoted per-head rate.

A full seated dinner with professional staffing and a menu rooted in Louisiana's culinary identity â€” Ã©touffÃ©e, red beans and rice elevated to banquet format, Gulf fish with local vegetables, and a bread pudding dessert that guests talk about on the flight home. Wedding.report's New Orleans data puts average per-guest spend at $205 to $372 depending on guest count; working backward to food-only catering at this service level runs approximately $72 to $108 per head before service charges.

Buffet and family-style service with a Louisiana character: a crawfish boil station, a red beans and rice buffet, a gumbo bar with corn bread, and fried catfish. The Balcony Ballroom's all-inclusive packages â€” which bundle catering, bar, and photography starting at $14,800 for 100 guests on a Sunday â€” give a sense of what bundled buffet-style catering costs in the New Orleans market. Heavy appetizers and food stations â€” oyster bar with local Gulf oysters, beignets dusted with powdered sugar, miniature muffulettas, and passed shrimp remoulade â€” rather than a seated meal. Deeply aligned with New Orleans' cocktail party culture, this format works beautifully at French Quarter courtyards, rooftop venues, and boutique hotel event spaces where standing and grazing is the natural register of the space.

A backyard or family property wedding where food comes from a trusted local institution â€” Central Grocery for muffulettas, CafÃ© Du Monde for beignets, or a neighborhood po'boy shop catering a casual spread. New Orleans' extraordinary neighborhood restaurant culture makes takeout-quality food genuinely exceptional at this tier. For anything at a formal venue with catering requirements, this option isn't available. For a 30-person courtyard gathering at a family home, it's very New Orleans.

Full-scale floral design in the New Orleans couture style â€” lush, layered, theatrical, rooted in French and Spanish colonial history. Large-scale floral design in the New Orleans style â€” magnolia branches, jasmine, anthurium, and tropical blooms with full ceremony and reception installations. Full installation at a historic mansion or hotel ballroom runs $10,000 to $17,000 at skilled New Orleans studios.

The full set of classic wedding florals with a New Orleans character: bridal bouquet with gardenias and trailing jasmine, ceremony arch, and reception centerpieces that lean into the city's romantic, slightly decadent aesthetic. Wedding.report puts New Orleans floral spend at $3,262 to $4,094 for 250 guests; a full traditional floral package at a French Quarter or Garden District venue for 100 to 150 guests runs $3,500 to $8,500.

A scaled-back floral plan paired with the inherent decor of New Orleans â€” iron balcony railings, exposed brick walls, Creole tile floors, and Spanish moss trailing from live oaks do more visual work than flowers in most settings. Candles, lanterns, and lush greenery runners complement the architectural character of New Orleans venues without requiring a full floral installation. Rental silk florals are increasingly popular in a humid subtropical climate where fresh flowers wilt faster than in northern markets.

Dried florals, magnolia branches from a family property, and Spanish moss arrangements. New Orleans' year-round subtropical greenery gives DIY arrangements strong raw material. The French Market on Decatur Street sells fresh cut flowers and seasonal botanicals at accessible prices. New Orleans is the birthplace of jazz, and wedding entertainment here is unlike anywhere in the country. A full 10 to 12-piece jazz or brass band for the evening, plus second line parade â€” a couple leading guests through the streets with handkerchiefs and parasols â€” with police escort and route coordination. A full reception jazz or brass band of 6 to 8 musicians in New Orleans, where live music and the second line tradition are unlike anywhere else. Full reception band plus second line combination runs $6,000 to $11,000 including the band's parade fee. City permit ($100) and police escort ($400 to $600) are separate.

A jazz trio or small brass ensemble for the ceremony and cocktail hour paired with a DJ for the reception â€” plus a second line brass band for the street parade between ceremony and reception. A professional wedding DJ for the full reception without a second line or live ensemble. Elysian Events notes DJ costs in Louisiana average around $100/hour; experienced New Orleans wedding DJs who understand the city's musical culture and can weave jazz, funk, and R&B into a reception playlist run $1,500 to $3,500 for a full evening.

A curated playlist managed by a trusted friend through a venue-provided sound system. Works for intimate courtyard ceremonies and small family property gatherings. Given New Orleans' musical culture â€” live music on virtually every corner â€” a DIY playlist at a wedding feels more like a missed opportunity here than in most cities, but it's a legitimate choice for micro-celebrations.

Lead photographer, second photographer, and a cinematographer â€” with dedicated second-line parade coverage from two simultaneous angles. A lead photographer, second shooter, and videography team for a full New Orleans wedding day â€” including second line coverage. A strong lead photographer paired with a highlight film videographer. A single experienced photographer, full-day coverage, no video. A trusted friend or newer photographer at an entry-level rate. Works for intimate courtyard ceremonies, micro-weddings at family properties, and elopements at City Park. Full-service planning in New Orleans requires local expertise that no amount of online research replaces: knowing which courtyard venues flood in a hard rain, which caterers have the right relationships with historic property owners, how to file second line parade permits, and how to coordinate police escorts without friction. Partial planning for couples who have booked their venue and key vendors but need local expertise for the final stages, second line logistics, and day-of management. Wedding.report puts New Orleans day-of coordination at $1,395 to $2,066 on average; experienced local coordinators who know the city's specific logistical constraints run $1,500 to $3,200.

No professional planning or coordination. Realistic for a small family courtyard gathering, a micro-wedding at City Park, or an intimate restaurant buyout where the venue manager handles the room. For anything involving a second line parade, a historic property, multiple outside vendors, or guests who don't know New Orleans â€” which describes most destination weddings here â€” the absence of a local coordinator creates meaningful day-of risk in a city that operates on its own schedule.

Bespoke letterpress or foil-stamped suites from New Orleans' boutique stationery designers â€” studios in the Magazine Street corridor and the Warehouse District arts community. A fully custom letterpress suite with save-the-dates, programs, menus, and escort cards runs $1,800 to $5,000.

Semi-custom and designer-template suites from Minted, Zola, or Artifact Uprising. A standard digitally printed suite of 100 sets runs $537 to $783 on Minted. Add save-the-dates and day-of paper goods, and a full package in this tier runs $450 to $1,800.

Paperless Post, Zola's digital invite tools, or a custom digital invite. Practical for destination weddings where guests are managing complex travel logistics and appreciate digital RSVP management. Free platforms are widely available; Paperless Post premium designs run $1 to $3 per send.

Word of mouth, a free Zola or The Knot wedding website, and personal outreach. Appropriate for intimate courtyard ceremonies, micro-weddings, and elopements. A Louisiana marriage license costs $27.50 at the Orleans Parish Clerk of Court â€” that's the only paper the state requires.

A full reception band of 6 to 8 musicians for a NYC wedding â€” soul group, jazz ensemble, or contemporary cover band. Bandwidth Entertainment puts the NYC average for live wedding bands at $10,000 to $20,000; skilled acts with Manhattan landmark venue experience run $15,000 to $24,000.

A live ensemble for ceremony and cocktail hour â€” a string quartet, jazz trio, or acoustic duo â€” paired with a DJ for the reception. Ensemble Music NYC and the New York String Ensemble are among the most-booked chamber groups for NYC weddings. This hybrid delivers the emotional weight of live music for the ceremony (a string quartet playing Shostakovich as the bridal party walks in) and the efficiency of a DJ for the dance floor. Budget $1,200 to $2,500 for the ensemble and $2,000 to $3,500 for a quality NYC wedding DJ.

A professional wedding DJ for the full reception. NT Wedding DJs and Porcci NYC both cite $2,000 to $4,000 as the standard range for an experienced NYC wedding DJ. At the lower end you're getting someone newer; at the upper end, DJs like DJ Reach bring MC experience, lighting programming, and crowd-reading ability from 60-plus weddings a year. For loft venues in Brooklyn and industrial spaces in Long Island City, a DJ â€” not a band â€” is almost always the right call both aesthetically and logistically.

A Spotify or Apple Music playlist managed by a trusted friend, run through a rented or venue-provided sound system. Works for intimate restaurant buyouts, backyard micro-weddings, and City Hall elopement dinners. The practical requirement: someone needs to own the music role for the evening and not get pulled away to socialize. Sound system rental from B&H Photo or local AV companies in NYC runs $200 to $500 for a speaker setup sufficient for a 30-person room.

Lead photographer, second photographer, and a cinematographer producing a feature film and highlight reel â€” with engagement session and a premium leather-bound album. Photographers like Sam Hurd, Christian Oth Studio, and KT Merry â€” whose work appears in Vogue Weddings â€” run $13,000 to $18,000 for the complete package. What you hire is a visual legacy: photographers with specific Rainbow Room and Cipriani experience who know exactly where to stand during the first dance to catch the 30 Rock skyline.

A lead photographer, second shooter, and videography team for a full NYC wedding day. Christian Oth's studio starts at $8,500 for photography alone; skilled NYC teams with landmark venue experience run $8,000 to $13,000. Manhattan's iconic architectural backdrop rewards photographers with deep local experience.

A strong lead photographer paired with a single videographer producing a highlight film â€” the combination most NYC couples in this budget settle on. Scratch Studios quotes most NYC couples $4,800 to $6,000 for photography alone at this level; adding a videographer producing a five- to eight-minute highlight film brings combined spend to $7,000 to $11,000. Photographers like Katie Beverley and studios in the Bushwick creative community work this tier â€” full-day coverage, 800-plus edited images, gallery within four to six weeks. You're getting someone who has shot Celestine, Liberty Warehouse, and The Weylin dozens of times and knows the light at each.

A single experienced photographer, full-day coverage, no video. Zola puts the NYC photography average at $5,000; The Knot's 2025 study aligns at $5,500. At this price point in NYC you're working with photographers building their portfolio at mid-tier venues â€” Greenpoint Loft, a restaurant buyout, Brooklyn Bridge Park â€” rather than the Rainbow Room. Photographers like Jessica Schilling and Ryan Ray NYC work this range. You typically get eight to ten hours of coverage, 500 to 700 edited images, and a four- to eight-week turnaround. No second shooter means ceremony and cocktail hour happening simultaneously is the primary trade-off.

A trusted friend with a capable camera, or a hobbyist photographer charging a nominal fee. The City Hall wedding market in NYC has created a real ecosystem of photographers specializing in small courthouse sessions â€” photographers like Elisa Bricker and Ryan and Alyssa NYC have built their practices around elopement work, typically charging $500 to $1,500 for a two- to four-hour session. For a Central Park micro-wedding or a DUMBO rooftop ceremony with 15 guests, this tier is entirely appropriate and can produce genuinely beautiful images in the right hands.

Full-service planning in NYC is a professional engagement from day one. Planners like Sheavonne Harris of Events by Sheavonne (22 years of NYC-specific experience, regularly at Cipriani and the Rainbow Room) and Laura Gelety of LLG Events (known for luxury Manhattan and Hamptons work) operate at $15,000 to $30,000 for full service. What that buys: a planner who has negotiated contracts with every major NYC venue, knows which caterers underperform at which rooms, can get your call returned at 583 Park when you can't, and has managed enough NYC-specific logistics â€” union labor rules at Cipriani, the Rainbow Room's specific vendor approval process â€” to keep your wedding from becoming a crisis.

Partial planning covers the final stretch: vendor sourcing for remaining categories, contract review, timeline creation, and full day-of management. Planners like Michelle Rago (specializing in the outer boroughs) and KNever Events work this tier. The primary value in NYC: contract review alone is worth the fee. Venue contracts run 12 to 20 pages and contain provisions â€” vendor approval clauses, F&B minimum shortfall penalties, force majeure language â€” that couples who haven't read hundreds of them miss.

Day-of coordination covers vendor confirmations, a detailed timeline, ceremony rehearsal management, and full execution from setup through breakdown. At Brooklyn loft and warehouse venues, the day-of coordinator is often the only thing standing between a beautiful wedding and a vendor-communication disaster â€” three caterers, a florist, a DJ, a photo team, and a venue staff all trying to load in through the same freight elevator between 9am and noon. NYC's market runs $1,500 to $4,000 given the additional logistical complexity compared to the national average.

No professional planning or coordination. Realistic for intimate gatherings of 20 or fewer, City Hall elopements, and micro-weddings at self-contained venues that include a venue coordinator in their fee. If your venue has an in-house coordinator (most hotels and dedicated venues do), confirm exactly what their scope covers â€” venue coordinators manage the venue's staff and logistics, not your vendors. That distinction matters enormously on the day.

Bespoke letterpress or foil-stamped invitation suites from Fox & Rose Press in Brooklyn, Bodega Press, and EAF Fine Paper â€” NYC's most respected specialty print studios. Bodega Press charges $18 to $24 per letterpress invitation set in short runs; a full suite for 100 guests typically runs $2,200 to $4,500. At the couture end, social stationers like Bernard Maisner on East 57th Street hand-letter invitations in copperplate calligraphy at $50 to $150 per piece for clients at the Rainbow Room and The Plaza.

Paperless Post, Zola's free digital invite tools, or a custom digital invite. Paperless Post's premium designs run $1 to $3 per send; a 100-guest list costs $100 to $300. For a rooftop micro-wedding or City Hall elopement dinner, digital invitations are entirely appropriate and often preferred by the tech-comfortable NYC guest demographic.

Word of mouth, a wedding website, and a group text. Entirely appropriate for elopements, City Hall ceremonies, and micro-weddings where guests are a tight circle. NYC's City Hall Marriage Bureau on Worth Street in Lower Manhattan processes several hundred marriages per day â€” the workflow is designed for exactly this kind of no-stationery wedding. A New York marriage license costs $35 â€” that's the only paper the state legally requires.

The Rainbow Room at 30 Rock, The Plaza, and Cipriani 42nd Street represent a category unto themselves â€” not venues you book but institutions you gain access to. Food and beverage minimums at the Rainbow Room start at $90,000; combined venue fee and minimum spend at The Plaza and Cipriani regularly reach $150,000-plus before a single vendor is hired. These spaces come with dedicated events directors, in-house production infrastructure, and a hundred years of Manhattan wedding history. Book 18 to 24 months out.

The New York Public Library's Astor Hall and Rose Main Reading Room, Gotham Hall in the former Greenwich Savings Bank, and Capitale at 130 Bowery Street represent historic Manhattan event spaces below the Rainbow Room/Plaza apex. Liberty Warehouse in Red Hook delivers Statue of Liberty views from the water's edge. Greenpoint Loft, 26 Bridge, and Erin McKenna's Art Factory offer dedicated event infrastructure with BYO catering flexibility that the hotel tier can't match.

Converted industrial buildings, artist studios, and raw loft spaces â€” Greenpoint Loft's smaller configurations, 501 Union in Gowanus, and the DIY-friendly warehouse venues in Bushwick and East Williamsburg. Most charge $3,000â€“$6,000 per day and permit outside catering, giving couples full control over the food budget while retaining a distinctive industrial-chic aesthetic. Expect exposed brick, concrete floors, and a blank-canvas approach that requires more planning but rewards creativity.

Celestine in DUMBO for up to 70 guests with the Manhattan Bridge filling the window; Il Buco in NoHo and The Smile in Nolita for 20â€“40 guests in intimate private rooms; Maialino at the Gramercy Park Hotel. A Tuesday-night Manhattan restaurant buyout typically runs $5,000â€“$15,000 all-in. Food and beverage minimum applies; the venue fee is usually nominal once the minimum is met.
